items.t: Wesfarmers stock faces retail test after RBA rate hike
sum: Wesfarmers stock faces a tougher retail backdrop after the Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate target on Tuesday, November 3. The stock traded at 49.80 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:32:32 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.
The latest quote is 1.78 percent below the 50.70 euros reported at 09:15 CET on November 5. This change since the previous report is separate from the daily comparison with an Xetra closing price.

The Reserve Bank of Australia statement said the Board increased the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 percent. Six members supported the move, while three voted to keep the rate at 4.60 percent.

The central bank said inflation was expected to remain elevated through much of 2027. It also said higher interest rates and falling housing prices and turnover were expected to weigh on household consumption.

Wesfarmers operates Bunnings, Kmart, Target and Officeworks alongside health, beauty and wellness businesses and industrial and resources operations. That diversification provides several earnings channels, but its major retail brands remain exposed to household budgets and housing activity.

The next signals for investors are trading updates covering customer traffic, comparable sales and margin protection. Bunnings is especially important because home-improvement demand can be affected by housing turnover, while general merchandise demand may weaken if higher repayments reduce discretionary spending.

Management's acquisition stance is another factor to watch. Wesfarmers has previously described potential deals across retail, lithium and chemicals as selective and disciplined, making execution and capital allocation relevant alongside near-term retail momentum.

Best ASX Retail Stocks to Watch in 2027: 6 Australian Shares With Momentum
sum: It has been a mixed reality for Australian retailers in 2026. On the one hand, supermarkets are experiencing increased demand for everyday essentials, while discretionary retailers are facing more cautious shoppers who are selective about where and how they spend.

Australian investors interested in ASX retail stocks are exposed to businesses across the divide, from those selling groceries and electronics to fashion and home appliances. This guide explores top ASX retail stocks with positive outlooks in 2027, their unique business strengths, and the factors to consider before investing in their retail shares.
ASX retail stocks are shares of companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) that generate revenue from selling goods and services to direct consumers.

These businesses operate across different categories such as groceries, electronics, clothing, homewares, beauty products, sporting goods, wearables, and more. As such, the country's largest supermarket chains and home-focused brands dominate the industry.
From an investment standpoint, publicly-listed retail businesses are categorised into two broad segments:

- Consumer stable brands: These are companies that sell everyday goods for individuals and households. Examples are supermarkets and food distributors that people patronise daily for food, groceries, and other essentials regardless of broader economic conditions.

- Consumer discretionary brands: These retailers sell products that consumers may not consider spending on immediately, depending on their budgets. Any product a consumer can postpone buying or spend less on due to interest rates, wages, employment conditions, and consumer confidence falls in this category. They include electronics, fashion items, furniture, and sporting goods.

sum: Wesfarmers stock traded at 48.72 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:00:31 CET on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, as the Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate to 4.85 percent. The rate decision was reported by PerthNow on Tuesday afternoon.

Six of the RBA's nine board members voted for a 25-basis-point increase, while three voted to leave rates unchanged. The decision keeps financing costs and household budgets in focus as Australian retailers enter the important Black Friday and Christmas trading period.

Wesfarmers owns Bunnings, Kmart and Officeworks, making consumer demand a central factor for the group's earnings outlook. The company's annual-meeting update on October 29 had already pointed to moderating Bunnings sales growth, particularly in seasonal and commercial categories. Kmart and Officeworks sales were described as broadly in line with the second half of fiscal 2026, while the group's mining operations provided an offset.

The latest rate decision adds a macroeconomic test to the company-specific retail signals. Higher borrowing costs can weigh on discretionary spending, while a resilient consumer environment would support the group's retail portfolio. The current news does not by itself establish the future direction of Wesfarmers stock.
The real-time quote of Wesfarmers stock was 48.72 euros at the stated Lang & Schwarz time.
Australian equities remained focused on the Reserve Bank's decision and its implications for household demand. Current market reports provide the broader market context.

Our view after Coles’ shares plunge
sum: Shares dropped 8% after reporting results for the September 2026 quarter.

Coles’ (ASX: COL) shares fell 8% after it reported core supermarket sales growth of 4% in the September 2026 quarter, similar to the growth achieved in the June 2026 quarter. Liquor sales declined 1% in the quarter, but sales momentum is improving.

Why it matters: Coles is underperforming archrival Woolworths, whose Australian supermarkets grew nearly twice as fast during the September quarter. We expect Coles to defend market share at the expense of profitability over the year.
- Guidance for flat first-half Supermarkets EBIT would preclude margin expansion, which we believe the market was expecting. We leave our flat EBIT margin forecast unchanged for fiscal 2027.

- The liquor segment continues to face headwinds from lower alcohol consumption, though sales declines are moderating. Even so, Coles is still losing share to industry leader Endeavour, whose sales grew 3% in the quarter.

The bottom line: We trim our fiscal 2027 sales forecast, but our earnings estimates are broadly unchanged, and we maintain our fair value estimate for no-moat Coles at $16.50 per share. Shares remain materially overvalued despite the fall following the September quarter update.

- Coles underperformed Woolworths over the past 12 months, but we expect it to match Woolworths’ deliberate discounting to reinvigorate sales momentum. Coles is flagging more discounts to boost sales, but we expect Woolworths to follow suit in real time.

Wesfarmers stock faces rate test as Bunnings outlook softens
sum: Wesfarmers stock enters the week of Monday, November 2, with Australian interest rates and retail demand in focus. The Reserve Bank of Australia is scheduled to meet on Tuesday, November 3, an event that FNArena describes as potentially market-moving.

FNArena's weekly preview says markets were pricing in an RBA rate hike on Melbourne Cup Day after September-quarter inflation confirmed persistent price pressure. The report also points to softer retail conditions and Wesfarmers' Bunnings update as part of a weaker consumer and housing backdrop.

The ASX 200 gained 1.8 percent during the week covered by FNArena, while remaining 3.67 percent below its 52-week high. That contrast leaves the rate decision as an important test for market sentiment, particularly for consumer-facing businesses.

Wesfarmers' annual-meeting update indicated that Bunnings sales growth had moderated, with weaker seasonal and commercial categories highlighted in the market coverage. Kmart and Officeworks sales were described as broadly in line with the second half of fiscal 2026, while mining operations provided a stronger offset.

The combination gives investors two issues to monitor: whether borrowing-cost expectations shift after the RBA meeting and whether the softer Bunnings trend extends into the wider Christmas trading period. Neither development by itself establishes the direction of the stock.

sum: Wesfarmers Ltd (ASX: WES) shares could be among the best options for dividends from an ASX blue-chip share.
One of the main reasons to like the company is its high-quality businesses, such as Bunnings, Kmart, Officeworks, WesCEF (chemicals, energy and fertilisers), and Priceline.
The company's profitability metrics really show how effective it is at making money.

In FY26, Wesfarmers reported a return on equity (ROE) of 35.5%, representing a 1.2 percentage point increase compared to FY25. Excluding significant items, it was a 4.3 percentage point rise for the ROE.
The return on capital (ROC) for its two key businesses is truly impressive. In FY26, Bunnings Group delivered a ROC of 69.2%, while Kmart Group's ROC was 68.3%.
Most businesses would love to achieve an ROC close to 70%, and that's exactly what the company delivers.
FY26 was a solid year for the company, with underlying earnings per share (EPS) climbing 8.3% and the dividend per Wesfarmers share being hiked by 7.8% to $2.22.

sum: Wesfarmers Ltd (ASX: WES) shares have fallen into the red on Thursday after the conglomerate posted its FY26 results ahead of the ASX open this morning.
At the time of writing, Wesfarmers shares are down around 2% and are changing hands at $81.38 a piece.
Today's price movement means the shares are now down around 1% for the year to date. They're also roughly 11% lower than 12 months ago.

The company reported a 3.4% increase in revenue, to $47.3 million, and a 7.3% increase in EBIT. But statutory NPAT fell 1.8% to $2.8 million including significant items, or was up 8.3% excluding them.
The result meant management was able to declare a full-year fully-franked ordinary dividend of 222 cents per share. This was a 15.8% increase from FY25.
The conglomerate saw strong performance across its major Bunnings and Kmart divisions, with earnings lifting 5.1% and 6% respectively over the 12-month period to 30th of June.
But elsewhere, Officeworks' earnings fell 22.2%, mainly due to one-off transformation costs.
